displayedInputs.question: Given \(\sqrt[3]{x-1}=-2\), find the value of \(x\).
Is \(\sqrt{2}\) rational or irrational?
Which of the following numbers is irrational?

Among the numbers \(3.14\), \(\sqrt{5}\), \(-\pi\), \(0.1010010001\ldots\) (with one more \(0\) between each successive pair of consecutive \(1\)s), \(\sqrt{16}\), \(22/7\), and \(\sqrt[3]{8}\), how many are irrational?
Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.B: All numbers written with a radical sign are irrational.
choices.C: All irrational numbers are nonterminating, nonrepeating decimals.
choices.D: The sum of two irrational numbers must be irrational.

displayedInputs.question: Near which location on the number line is \(\pi\)?
Among the real numbers \(-2\), \(0\), \(\sqrt{3}\), \(1/2\), \(\pi\), and \(-\sqrt{9}\), how many are rational?
How many integers have an absolute value less than \(\sqrt{10}\)?
Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: Real numbers correspond one-to-one with points on the number line.
choices.B: All points on the number line represent rational numbers.
choices.C: Real numbers are divided into two categories: positive real numbers and negative real numbers.

displayedInputs.question: Estimate which two integers \(\sqrt{10}\) lies between. (Enter the smaller integer.)
\(\sqrt{30}\) lies between two consecutive integers. What is the larger integer?
Which comparison between \(\sqrt{5}\) and \(2.2\) is correct?
\(\sqrt{47}-2\) lies between two consecutive integers. What is the smaller integer?
How many integers \(n\) satisfy \(\sqrt{11}<n<\sqrt{90}\)?
Calculate \(\sqrt{9}+\sqrt[3]{(-8)}-|1-\sqrt{2}|\).
Calculate \(\sqrt{16}+\sqrt[3]{27}-\sqrt{4}\).
Given \(\sqrt{3}\approx1.732\), calculate an approximate value of \(2\sqrt{3}-1\), rounding the result to the nearest \(0.01\).
Do the movie ticket labels “row 3, seat 5” and “row 5, seat 3” refer to the same seat?

choices.A: They refer to the same seat.

displayedInputs.question: Seats are represented by (column, row). Xiaoming is in column 3, row 5, written as \((3,5)\). How is the seat in column 5, row 3 written?

Seats are represented by (column, row), with row numbers increasing from front to back. Xiaoming sits at \((3,4)\), and Xiaoliang sits in the seat immediately behind him, represented by \((a,b)\). Find \(a,b\) (separate your answers with a comma).
If the ordered pairs \((2x-1,5)\) and \((x+2,5)\) represent the same position, find the value of \(x\).
How do you plot the point \((-2,3)\) in the coordinate system?

choices.A: From the origin, move 2 units right, then 3 units up.
choices.B: From the origin, move 3 units left, then 2 units up.
choices.C: From the origin, move 2 units right, then 3 units down.
choices.D: From the origin, move 2 units left, then 3 units up.

displayedInputs.question: Write the x-coordinate and y-coordinate of the point \(P(4,-5)\) (answer in that order, separated by a comma).
What are the distances from the point \(P(-3,4)\) to the x-axis and the y-axis, respectively? (Separate your answers with a comma.)

Point \(P\) is in the fourth quadrant. Its distance to the x-axis is \(2\), and its distance to the y-axis is \(5\). Let the coordinates of \(P\) be \((a,b)\). Find \(a,b\) (separate your answers with a comma).
In which quadrant is the point \((-3,-1)\)? (Enter the number 1, 2, 3, or 4.)
Which of the following points is in the second quadrant?
Point \(P(m-2,2m+4)\) lies on the x-axis. Find the value of \(m\).
If point \(P(a,b)\) is in the fourth quadrant, in which quadrant is point \(Q(-b,a)\)? (Enter the number 1, 2, 3, or 4.)
Where is point \(A(0,-3)\) located?
Given \(A(1,2)\) and \(B(1,6)\), find the length of \(AB\).
Given \(A(-3,2)\) and \(B(4,2)\), find the length of \(AB\).
The vertices of triangle \(ABC\) are \(A(0,0)\), \(B(4,0)\), and \(C(1,3)\). Find the area of the triangle.
To describe the locations of landmarks on campus, how should the origin be chosen for convenience?

choices.A: Choose the most remote corner as the origin and do not specify a unit
choices.B: Choose a prominent location, such as the flagpole or school gate, as the origin and specify the unit length
choices.C: Set up a separate coordinate system for each landmark
choices.D: Do not set up a coordinate system; describe locations only using “left” and “right”

displayedInputs.question: Set up a coordinate system with the school flagpole as the origin, due east as the positive x-direction, and due north as the positive y-direction, with 1 unit representing 10 m. The library is 30 m due east and 40 m due north of the flagpole. Its coordinates are \((a,b)\). Find \(a\) and \(b\) (separate your answers with commas).

Use the school flagpole as the origin, due east as the positive x-direction, and due north as the positive y-direction, with 1 unit representing 10 m. The classroom building has coordinates \((-2,3)\). How many meters due west and how many meters due north of the flagpole is it? (Unit: m. Answer in that order, separated by commas.)

Use the school flagpole as the origin, due east as the positive x-direction, and due north as the positive y-direction, with 1 unit representing 10 m. The cafeteria has coordinates \((3,-4)\), and the dormitory has coordinates \((3,2)\). How many meters apart are they? (Unit: m.)
Point \(A(2,3)\) is first translated 4 units to the left and then 1 unit upward. What are its new coordinates? (Write the x-coordinate followed by the y-coordinate, separated by a comma.)
